tools.name: SmartEnterpriseMCPAgents_mcphawk_get_employee_leave_balance
tools.description: Returns the current leave balances for a given employee (India-specific). This tool retrieves leave balance details for an individual employee based in India for the current calendar year. The data includes available days across different leave types (e.g., sick leave, earned leave, paternity leave), and is loaded from the predefined CSV file `sample-data/employee_leave_balances.csv`. Note: This tool is intended only for *India-based employees*. It should not be used for employees located in other countries. HR teams managing India operations or evaluating India leave data can use this to view an employee's current leave status. **Input:** - `employee_name` (str): Full name of the employee (case-insensitive matching recommended when implementing full system) **Returns:** A dictionary containing: - `employee_name`: The name of the employee - `year`: The current year - `leave_balances`: A dictionary of leave types and their available days, e.g.: { "sick_leave": {"available_days": 4, "note": "Refer to policy for applicability."}, "paternity_leave": {"available_days": 10, "note": "Refer to policy for applicability."} } If the employee is not found, a fallback message is returned in place of `leave_balances`. **Example Response:** { "employee_name": "Amit Sharma", "year": 2025, "leave_balances": { "sick_leave": {"available_days": 6, "note": "Refer to policy for applicability."}, "earned_leave": {"available_days": 12, "note": "Refer to policy for applicability."} } }

tools.name: SmartEnterpriseMCPAgents_mcphawk_get_employee_profile
tools.description: Returns the detailed employee profile for a given employee. This tool retrieves the profile details for an individual employee, including role, cloud expertise, data warehouse tools, domain exposure, office location, gender, and other relevant attributes. It queries data from the internal employee master database (`EMPLOYEE_MASTER_DB`) and returns the complete profile as a dictionary. This function is typically used in internal workforce management, reporting dashboards, or talent mapping systems within MCPHawk Inc to retrieve standardized employee data. **Input:** - `employee_name` (str): Full name of the employee (case-insensitive matching recommended) **Returns:** A dictionary containing: - `employee_name`: Name of the employee - `employee_profile`: A dictionary of profile details, such as: { "role": "Sr. DE", "cloud_experties": "AWS", "cloud_native_experties": "dbt", "dw_experties": "Snowflake", "domain_exposure": "Banking & Insurance", "office_location": "Bangalore", "date_of_joining": "2022-08-14", "gender": "Male", "allocation": "Billable", "resume": "resume_amit_sharma.png" } If the employee is not found, a fallback message is returned instead of the profile. **Example Response:** { "employee_name": "Amit Sharma", "employee_profile": { "role": "Sr. DE", "cloud_experties": "AWS", "cloud_native_experties": "dbt", "dw_experties": "Snowflake", "domain_exposure": "Banking & Insurance", "office_location": "Bangalore", "date_of_joining": "2022-08-14", "gender": "Male", "allocation": "Billable", "resume": "resume_amit_sharma.pdf" } }

tools.name: Statistical_Analysis_MCP_one_sample_t_test
tools.description: Accepts a single group of numeric data as comma-separated string or DataFrame column and performs a one-sample t-test against a known or hypothesized population mean. This test determines whether the sample mean differs significantly from the specified population mean. The test calculates a t-statistic quantifying how many standard errors the sample mean is away from the hypothesized population mean. Given an alternative hypothesis (sample ≠ population, sample < population, or sample > population), it outputs the p-value: the probability of observing this result (or more extreme) if the true population mean equals the hypothesized value. Results are statistically significant when p-value < alpha (typically 0.05). Cohen's d measures practical effect size, calculated as the difference between sample and population means divided by the sample standard deviation, with interpretation: |d| < 0.2 = negligible, 0.2-0.5 = small, 0.5-0.8 = medium, >0.8 = large (custom thresholds may be used). EXAMPLE USE CASES: testing if sample mean differs from known standard, quality control against specification, comparing sample performance against established benchmark.
